hook_text: At midnight, the sales pages burn to zero. One list walks through untouched.
clip_script: Midnight, last day of February. The year's report card is written; the profit has gone home to the owner's jar. Now watch the books as the clock strikes. The STORY pages — sales, every expense, every income — burn down to zero. Not lost: promoted. A whole year compressed into one number living in Capital. They must start empty — March's sales need a clean page, or no one could ever say what the new year earned. But one list walks straight through midnight: everything the shop OWNS, everything it OWES, the owner's stake. The bakkie doesn't stop existing at midnight. The loan doesn't forgive itself. Owning continues — only earning starts fresh. That surviving list is the post-closing trial balance — and here's the twist: this year's ending is literally next year's beginning. The cycle closes into itself. That's why they call it a cycle.
visual_style: A ledger at a stroke-of-midnight clock: nominal pages igniting into embers that stream into a jar labelled Capital, while one glowing page floats through the midnight line intact into a new blank book.
pacing: Slow clock build, fast burn montage, serene close on the surviving page becoming page one.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and close a year properly — then open the next.
